title: NLTK dependency graph rendering can execute a planted Graphviz binary
summary: dot2img resolves Graphviz dot without the trusted executable ownership checks or environment scrubbing used by other NLTK wrappers. A local attacker can plant a binary in a writable PATH directory for execution as the rendering user.

severity.rationale: Exploitation needs local write access to a directory on the victim process PATH and dependency graph rendering. These local prerequisites support a 30-day response despite the possible code execution.

affected.note: Versions through 3.10.3 are affected. Advisory headers and the reviewed database identify 3.10.4 as patched; older fix-status paragraphs in the advisory describe pre-release work.

exposure: POSIX processes calling dot2img or rendering a DependencyGraph in a notebook are exposed when an attacker can replace dot in a directory on their PATH.

remediation.action: Upgrade NLTK and protect executable search paths
remediation.details: Use NLTK 3.10.4 or later. Remove group/world-writable directories from the rendering process PATH and keep Graphviz in a directory writable only by the user or root.
remediation.risk: The release tightens data-path and external-tool checks; legitimate integrations may need adjustment.

verification: Confirm the loaded NLTK version is 3.10.4 or later and test dependency graph rendering with trusted Graphviz.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
